title: The fifth condition of Salah – facing the Qiblah
intro: Muslims all over the world face the Ka‘bah in Makkah when they pray.

learn.html: The fifth condition of Salah is facing the Qiblah. The Qiblah is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah, in Arabia. Muslims all over the world face it when they pray.

The Ka‘bah is the first and most honoured house of Allah, in the city of Makkah. It is a stone building shaped like a cube, with a flat roof and no windows. In one corner is the black stone – al-Hajar al-Aswad. Every year the Ka‘bah is covered with a black cloth with ayahs of the Qur’an written on it.

Around the Ka‘bah is the Haram, the holy area where Muslims from all over the world pray, recite the Qur’an and do tawaf – walking around the Ka‘bah – during Hajj. The Ka‘bah and the Haram are the most honoured place on earth for all Muslims.

learn.title: Where is the Qiblah from here?
learn.html: From Bosnia the Qiblah is to the south-east. From Erie, in North America, the Qiblah is roughly to the north-east – use a compass or a Qiblah app to be exact.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: If we don’t know the direction of the Qiblah, we try to find out and then face where we think it is. We must not pray toward a figure, picture or photo of a person or animal.
